subject: MGCFA common factor model with lavaan (unequal df for models which should have equal df)

messages.author: d761cfe2b7d71483
messages.subject: MGCFA common factor model with lavaan (unequal df for models which should have equal df)
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to replicate the MGCFA results from Dolan (2000) with lavaan. The common factor model I built is explained at pages 27-28 and Table 3 (see 1st order aMGCFMs and footnote e) of the paper. Basically, it involves that the loadings, intercepts, residuals are equal across groups. And then, among the three correlated latent factors, (one or) two of them have free latent mean differences (π) and free variance/covariance matrix (Δ).

My problem is this :

In Dolan's paper, table 4, all models C4, C5, and C6 have df=152. This is logical because in C4, PERF and MEM are free, while in C5 it's PERF and VERB and for C6 it's MEM and VERB factors. But when I tried it in lavaan, I got df=152, df=153, df=153 for C4, C5 and C6 models, respectively. And I can't detect the source of the error.

I hope you can clarify this for me. Thanks !

The syntax :

(For C4 (or commonfactor4), group differences are explained by PERF and MEM factors. For C5, group differences are explained by PERF and VERB factors. For C6, group differences are explained by MEM and VERB factors.)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MGCFA common factor model with lavaan (unequal df for models which should have equal df)
parts: You can see the problem by looking at the parameter tables (or other outputs from lavInspect, such as "free" or "partable") to check your constraints.  For example:

commonfactor4.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor4.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"), group.partial=c("PERF~~PERF", "MEM~~MEM", "PERF~~MEM"))

commonfactor4.fit@ParTable # or in matrix form using:   lavInspect(commonfactor4.fit, "partable")

Here you can see that the latent covariance "PERF~~MEM" is not constrained across groups because they do not contain the same label in the "label" column (lavaan assigns labels for simple equality constraints even if they aren't specified by the user in the syntax).

commonfactor5.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor5.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"), group.partial=c("PERF~~PERF", "VERB~~VERB", "PERF~~VERB"))

commonfactor5.fit@ParTable

Here you can see that the latent covariance "PERF~~VERB" is mistakenly constrained across groups because the order in the parameter table is "VERB~~PERF", which is arbitrary.  You can fix this by changing the order in your "group.partial" argument.

commonfactor6.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor6.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"), group.partial=c("MEM~~MEM", "VERB~~VERB", "MEM~~VERB"))

commonfactor6.fit@ParTable

Here, you can see the same thing happens.  You can fix it by changing "MEM~~VERB" to "VERB~~MEM" in your "group.partial" argument.  

The order of names in a covariance specification should be arbitrary, but specifying both is redundant, so the parameter table can only include one line.  I'm guessing the order is based on the order in which the latent variables were defined in the model syntax (maybe the same for observed variables?).  I wonder whether Yves could add a check for this when the "group.partial" argument is used.  I also wonder whether this problem would have happened at all if you had not used the "group.partial" argument, but rather freed the equality constraints explicitly in your model syntax:

combined.commonfactor5.model <-'
VERB =~ Information + Similarities + Arithmetic + Vocabulary + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement
PERF =~ Similarities + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement + BlockDesign + ObjectAssembly + Coding + Mazes
MEM =~ Information + Arithmetic + DigitSpan + TappingSpan + BlockDesign + Coding + Mazes
MEM ~ 0*1

PERF ~~ c(NA, NA)*PERF + c(NA, NA)*VERB
VERB ~~ c(NA, NA)*VERB
'

Perhaps the syntax parser already automatically puts the variables in the right order, so either order could be used to the same effect:

combined.commonfactor5.model <-'
VERB =~ Information + Similarities + Arithmetic + Vocabulary + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement
PERF =~ Similarities + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement + BlockDesign + ObjectAssembly + Coding + Mazes
MEM =~ Information + Arithmetic + DigitSpan + TappingSpan + BlockDesign + Coding + Mazes
MEM ~ 0*1

PERF ~~ c(NA, NA)*PERF
VERB ~~ c(NA, NA)*VERB + c(NA, NA)*PERF
'

Terry

Thanks for the answer, both of you. I understand now why I never had problems when I use MGCFA on the Woodcock-Johnson (I attached the syntax). And indeed, in the above data set used by Dolan (2000), when the order of the latent vars in group.partial corresponds to the order of the latent vars in the model syntax, all of these competing models have equal df, as one should expect.

Although I have tried the syntax suggested by Terrence Jorgensen, e.g.,

combined.commonfactor5.model <-'
VERB =~ Information + Similarities + Arithmetic + Vocabulary + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement
PERF =~ Similarities + Comprehension + PictureCompletion + PictureArrangement + BlockDesign + ObjectAssembly + Coding + Mazes
MEM =~ Information + Arithmetic + DigitSpan + TappingSpan + BlockDesign + Coding + Mazes

MEM ~ 0*1
PERF ~~ c(NA, NA)*PERF + c(NA, NA)*VERB
VERB ~~ c(NA, NA)*VERB
'

commonfactor5.fit<-cfa(combined.commonfactor5.model, sample.cov=combined.cov, sample.nobs=combined.n, sample.mean=combined.means, meanstructure=TRUE, group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "residuals", "lv.variances"))
fitMeasures(commonfactor5.fit, fit.measures="all")

 I got :

Error in getModifier(rhs[[3L]][[2L]]) : 
  lavaan ERROR: can not parse modifier:cNANA

I don't know the reason. In any case, the first method works. I will just need to be careful about the order of the variables.
